name: The memory wash
desc: A roadside museum copying Trump’s Smithsonian history order has installed a “patriotic rinse.” Your crew is invited to test it with a public eviction account. The dryer returns a story about families discovering fresh air. One sock still contains a bailiff.

choices.label: Use your paper; document the rinse

effects.log: You use some supplies tracing every altered line, head pounding. The original account survives. The dryer requests a gentler historical cycle.

choices.label: Let the rinse improve your account

effects.log: The cleaned-up account is soothing and wrong. A resident points out that “voluntary camping” began when the locks changed.
You repeat the display’s version and get corrected. The resident brings a key. It fits the history considerably better than the caption.

name: Smaller government
desc: DOGE fired the park’s cleaners. The remaining ranger hasn’t had lunch. She offers your crew gloves beside overflowing bins. “Congratulations. You’re the smaller government.”

choices.label: Share some food and help clear the bins

effects.log: You share lunch and haul bags until your back aches. She hands you a bin liner. “Uniform allowance.”

choices.label: Photograph the mess for your D.C. case

effects.log: You photograph the overflowing bins. She points at the flies. “Only department still recruiting.”

name: Supporting dinner
desc: At a pantry preparing for the 2025 SNAP cuts, volunteers welcome your hungry crew and any help you can spare. A senator’s tax-cut leaflet props up the short table leg. It’s finally supporting dinner.

effects.log: You eat and take some food. The tax-cut leaflet stays under the table; removing it would cost everyone their lunch.
You record the volunteers and collect some food. They ask you to include the casserole before Washington counts it as unnecessary spending.
You donate some food. A volunteer tapes your receipt over the senator’s smile. The first thing on that leaflet that fed anyone.

name: Closing-time education
desc: Trump ordered steps toward closing the Education Department. At a PTA fundraiser, parents ask your stopped crew to feed the volunteers or record their mock clearance sale. A desk is labelled “POWER RETURNED TO PARENTS.” Two parents are arguing over how to lift it.

choices.label: Share some food; join the sale

effects.log: You share some food and join the parents’ mock auction. The desk goes to whoever can explain long division without crying.
You record the display for D.C. The chair marked “local control” still has a federal assembly diagram taped underneath.
You leave some supplies and settle into the reading corner. The book opens without anyone first abolishing its publisher.

name: Unmanaged wilderness
desc: After the DOGE park firings, neighbors are clearing a picnic shelter that maintenance staff used to handle. They wave your van over for help. A vine has reached the visitor-information window. It’s the first applicant willing to work for sunlight.

effects.log: You drag branches until your shoulders ache. Everyone cheers when the picnic table emerges. It has survived its promotion to wilderness.
You donate some supplies; volunteers add your contribution to their account. The rake’s new handle makes it the park’s best-supported employee.
You record who did the maintenance before the firings. A squirrel interrupts. The volunteer refuses to list it as a contractor.

name: Return to nonexistent sender
desc: At a library stop, volunteers give your crew letters about the nonexistent studies in the first MAHA report. They offer some food for an accurate recorded reply. A retired postman has brought an empty envelope. “That’s all the research we could fit.”

effects.log: You read and save the letters, laughing. The postman has underlined “address unknown” so hard the nonexistent study now has a window.
You record the citation corrections and collect some food. The librarian checks the reply exists before pressing play.
You share some food and sort the letters with the volunteers. Every missing study gets a real paperclip. The science budget is recovering.

name: The coverage ladder
desc: At a health-funding teach-in, volunteers show your stopped crew how the 2025 Medicaid law changes eligibility and spending. They’ve built a demonstration ladder. The bottom rung is labelled “taxpayer.” The first reachable rung has been removed to keep the model affordable.

effects.log: You check the sources and understand the changes. The volunteer restores the missing rung for packing. Even the demonstration needs it to work.
You enjoy the rehearsal. The volunteer playing a senator praises the ladder from a stepladder somebody else brought.

name: Imported freedom
desc: Trump’s tariffs have raised a tool co-op’s replacement bill. At your roadside stop, the owner offers $10 and some food for shifting repairable stock. Donated supplies would also help. A broken imported drill is being guarded by a perfectly American padlock.

effects.log: You donate some supplies; the co-op records your contribution. The imported drill can finally be repaired using something cheaper than a patriotic speech.
You earn $10 and some food, sore but laughing. The owner locks the empty crate. “Still cheaper to insure than replace.”
You share some food and record the changed bills. The owner points to the lunch. “Our first import today without a surcharge.”

name: Patriotic cartography
desc: Trump’s Gulf renaming has left a roadside map club with old charts and new federal labels. They ask your stopped crew to help prepare a public comparison. The volunteer has carefully checked the coast. It has made no effort to move.

effects.log: You donate some supplies and help document the labels. The volunteer uses a ruler to confirm that greatness added no coastline.

choices.label: Share some food with the club

effects.log: You share some food, and everyone invents patriotic names for the crumbs. The plate becomes the first disputed territory to disappear.
You compare and save the charts, relieved to find the coordinates unchanged. The volunteer gives the compass permission to remain neutral.

name: Visitor disinformation
desc: After DOGE park staffing cuts, volunteers are making their own visitor guide. They wave your crew into the turnout and offer some food for hauling display boards. The official welcome mural has six smiling rangers. The actual ranger is asking the mural for directions.

effects.log: You document the volunteers’ guide and its sources. The ranger circles a working restroom. The mural’s career advice remains disappointing.

choices.label: Haul the boards for some food

effects.log: You earn some food and a sore shoulder hauling boards. The painted rangers continue their excellent attendance record without lifting anything.
You laugh through the ranger’s tour. She introduces the painted staff individually. All six have apparently chosen to work remotely.

name: The people's megaphone
desc: At a roadside fair, residents protesting unlimited independent political spending ask your crew for testimony or help pushing their parade float. The float is a megaphone stuffed with imitation banknotes. It takes four people to make money talk.

effects.log: You add your testimony to the residents’ record. The volunteer puts it beside the megaphone. Your voice has arrived without a forklift.
You push until your shoulders ache, laughing with the residents. The giant megaphone finally speaks: its wheel squeaks all the way downhill.

name: The cost of the plug
desc: Your crew stops at a public briefing on the Trump administration’s proposed NIH overhead cap. A researcher has brought itemized costs, chairs, and an unplugged freezer to explain what “overhead” pays for. The demonstration ice is providing a floor-level impact assessment.

effects.log: You verify the figures with a headache. The researcher adds electricity to the example. The ice has already submitted its objection.
You sit and ease your sore legs. The researcher quietly plugs in a fan. Overhead immediately improves conditions for the taxpayer.
You save the dated estimate and its proposal status. The researcher sets the papers above the puddle. That shelf is overhead too.

name: Approved memories
desc: Your crew stops at a town museum’s public review, modelled on Trump’s Smithsonian history order. A board member wants an eviction photograph retitled “Family Relocation.” Former residents are waiting to speak. The family’s furniture is still visibly on the pavement.

effects.log: You defend the dated account, head aching. The board member proposes cropping out the sofa. History is improving one cushion at a time.
You stop arguing and repeat the caption. A former resident corrects you: people usually get to choose where they relocate the refrigerator.
You rest outside and enjoy the quiet. Through the window, the board keeps moving the caption. The sofa hasn’t moved an inch.

name: The eight-dollar gulf
desc: A marina sign shop offers your stopped crew $8 to check labels following Trump’s federal Gulf renaming. The printer also welcomes witnesses to the old-and-new comparison. The label that says “America” costs more than the patch keeping the boat afloat.

effects.log: You learn the difference and laugh at the samples. The printer holds the old label over a leak. It remains impressively seaworthy.

choices.label: Use your paper; record the changes

effects.log: You use some supplies to record the changes accurately. The marina’s coordinates fit on one line. Greatness requires a second sheet.
You earn $8 and settle the spelling. The printer sticks the new name on a bucket. It still needs emptying.

name: Break-room government
desc: Your hot, aching crew stops beside a travelling roofers’ protest against Florida’s ban on local heat mandates. Volunteers have shade and towels but need water. Their display shows a politician praising freedom from regulation beneath an umbrella held by somebody else.

effects.log: You use some water and recover in the shade. The volunteer wrings out a towel. Individual responsibility has soaked the bucket.
You record the Florida rule and the roofers’ account. The display’s politician has a permanent parasol; everyone else has a shift rota.
You leave some water for the workers. A roofer pours it into the cooler without first checking whether the county approved compassion.

name: One person, one microphone
desc: Residents at a roadside civic picnic are challenging unlimited super-PAC money with accounts from ordinary voters. They welcome your crew’s story and share food for the trip. A donor has lent a powerful loudspeaker. He keeps asking whether it can make him the electorate.

choices.label: Add your account to the record

effects.log: You add your account and enjoy the residents’ applause. The donor tests the microphone. It still produces only one person.

choices.label: Take some food for the road

effects.log: You collect some food. The cook gives everyone the same portion. The loudspeaker donor asks whether she has heard how loudly he contributes.

choices.label: Share some food; join the picnic

effects.log: You share some food and enjoy the picnic. The donor’s speech competes with a crisp packet. The packet has better timing.

name: The protected soup tin
desc: Trump’s tariffs have raised a community canner’s packaging bill. At your road stop, she asks for donated supplies or help shifting crates in exchange for some food. She holds up a tin. “This is the bit we’ve made too expensive to throw away.”

effects.log: You donate some supplies, and she records your help. The soup can now reach people without needing its own investment prospectus.
You haul crates until your arms ache and earn some food. The canner asks you to bring back the tins before retiring on them.

name: The freedom treadmill
desc: A travelling trade fair celebrates Florida’s ban on local heat mandates with a “voluntary break” treadmill. Your hot crew stops beside it. The water cooler moves farther away whenever the belt turns. A roofer offers shade and asks for water donations.

choices.label: Use some water; rest in shade

effects.log: You use some water and recover beside the roofer. The treadmill records your stationary body as a troubling decline in productivity.
You stumble off with sore shins. The operator congratulates you on freely choosing to approach the cooler, which has reached the next county.

choices.label: Donate some water; document the display

effects.log: You donate some water and document the display with the roofer. The cooler becomes accessible as soon as someone unplugs freedom.

name: Gift capacity
desc: After the Pentagon accepted Qatar’s luxury jet, a roadside workers’ fair built a gift-inspection tunnel. Your crew is invited to compare it with their employer’s strict gift rule. A muffin cannot pass. The aircraft-shaped hole behind it is generously proportioned.

choices.label: Use your paper; record the comparison

effects.log: You use some supplies to save the jet report and workplace rule. The inspector measures the muffin again. Still dangerously low altitude.

choices.label: Donate supplies; help decorate the tunnel

effects.log: You donate some supplies and enjoy decorating the tunnel. The muffin gets cardboard wings. The inspector suddenly requires a much smaller ruler.

choices.label: Watch from the quiet picnic table

effects.log: You relax at the picnic table. The inspector walks around the aircraft-shaped hole searching for small gifts. The muffin remains under heavy guard.

name: The accidental recipient booth
desc: A roadside technology fair recreates the Trump officials’ Signal scandal using sandwich plans. Your crew can inspect the recipient list. The demonstration journalist gets every detail. The person making lunch receives a message saying the schedule is too sensitive.

effects.log: You verify the demonstration against the reported scandal. The sandwich maker finally gets the order by asking the journalist what’s for lunch.

choices.label: Trace and save the message sequence

effects.log: You save the sequence with a headache. The operator adds another padlock to the lunch box. The message list remains wide open.

choices.label: Post that nobody else saw it

effects.log: You post the wrong claim and get corrected. The demonstration journalist has already described the sandwich, its departure time, and the pickle.

name: Return to sender
desc: Trump’s order to facilitate closing the Education Department has inspired a roadside “power returned to parents” booth. Your crew is handed an enormous demonstration parcel. Inside are unpaid tasks. The volunteer has helpfully attached a return label addressed to the parent holding it.

effects.log: You document the proposal and question every task, head aching. The volunteer folds the return label into a circle. Local control is complete.
You clear your head outside the demonstration. The parcel passes between parents. Nobody can find the end marked “empowerment.”

choices.label: Announce the department is already abolished

effects.log: You enjoy a simpler story until a teacher corrects you: the closure directive wasn’t an act of Congress. Your parcel needs another label.

name: The patriotic billfold
desc: Trump’s tariffs have made a hardware importer’s invoice long enough to carpet his roadside shop. He invites your crew to inspect it. The charge paid by Americans runs past the till. The part where foreigners reimburse him is still awaiting delivery.

choices.label: Check and save the invoice trail

effects.log: You save the verified bill, head aching from following it. The importer rolls up the reimbursement section. It’s the cardboard tube.

choices.label: Use your paper; record the charges

effects.log: You use some supplies to document the charges accurately. The importer marks the American payer. You no longer need the entire floor plan.
You clear your head outside. The importer closes the door carefully so it doesn’t pinch the part of the bill that bought the handle.

name: The employed calendar
desc: A roadside benefits workshop previews Medicaid work checks due from 2027. Your crew is invited to inspect its calendar machine. It stamps every working day “prove it,” then adds a new day for proving it. The cleaner’s week has developed an extension.

choices.label: Check and save the rollout dates

effects.log: You save the actual rollout dates and clear up the confusion. The cleaner removes the extra day. It still appears on the paperwork.

choices.label: Report that the federal rollout already happened

effects.log: You repeat the premature claim and get corrected. The calendar machine has confused preparing for the deadline with surviving it.

choices.label: Use your paper; copy the rules

effects.log: You use some supplies to copy the rules accurately. The volunteer puts the extra day in a folder. It no longer fits the week.

name: The unquestioning entrance
desc: A fairground classroom inspired by Trump’s anti-indoctrination order admits questions only after they pass a patriotism test. Your crew stops at the gate. The test asks whether you agree with the test. A short exit slide is marked for people who already do.

choices.label: Use your paper; challenge the lesson

effects.log: You use some supplies documenting the proposal and arguing through the test until your head pounds. Your evidence gets detention for asking follow-ups.

choices.label: Agree; take the quick exit slide

effects.log: You scrape an elbow on the slide and feel done with it. A teacher corrects your claim that patriotic approval proves historical accuracy.

choices.label: Leave without taking the parents’ account

effects.log: You clear your head and leave without the parents’ evidence. The gate counts another visitor who has declined to question it.

name: The ordinary-voter table
desc: Your crew stops at a diner staging a version of Trump’s meme-coin investor dinner. The ordinary-voter table is behind three velvet ropes. The host offers to explain access. The cutlery has arrived by limousine; the people who wash it are still outside.

choices.label: Check the dinner report with workers

effects.log: You verify the investor-access account, head aching. A dishwasher asks the host to introduce him as the person who holds all the forks.
You clear your head at the quiet counter. The host upgrades a spoon to the private room. It has excellent silver holdings.
You nap and miss the workers’ account. When you wake, the cutlery has finished its exclusive reception. The dishwashers are still waiting.

name: The mint with foreign ties
desc: Your crew stops at a temp-work desk. The recruiter’s no-gifts briefing runs beneath a report about the Pentagon accepting Qatar’s jet. She seals a complimentary mint in an evidence bag. “Vendor influence.” The mint has achieved a level of scrutiny unavailable to most aircraft.

choices.label: Use your paper; record the comparison

effects.log: You use some supplies to save the workplace rule and jet report. The recruiter weighs the mint again. Its influence remains pocket-sized.
You clear your head outside. Through the window, the recruiter is still completing the mint’s chain of custody.

choices.label: Repeat that every gift is allowed

effects.log: You repeat the false blanket claim and get corrected. The recruiter points to the workplace rule. The mint remains detained pending lunch.

name: The unpaid view
desc: After DOGE park staff cuts, local volunteers have reopened a picnic area for the afternoon. Your crew is welcome to rest; donated supplies help them manage it. The visitor brochure calls the view priceless. The volunteer has priced the toilet paper separately.

choices.label: Donate some supplies to the volunteers

effects.log: You donate some supplies, and the volunteers note your help. A roll goes straight to the restroom. The view remains completely unbothered.
You rest and clear your head without using supplies. The volunteer turns the brochure face down. The actual view has better staffing.

name: Uniformly absent
desc: At a park stop after DOGE firings, volunteers offer your crew some food and ask for help sorting abandoned service-desk stock. A rack holds uniforms for staff who aren’t coming back. It has more name badges than the welcome desk.

effects.log: You haul stock until your shoulders and head ache. The ranger finds another uniform. It is immediately qualified to staff the empty desk.
You record the staffing account and laugh at the ranger’s coat-hanger demonstration. The hangers achieve perfect attendance while declining every visitor request.

choices.label: Take some food for the road

effects.log: You take some food from the visitors’ donation. It’s the only queue today with somebody working at both ends.

name: Lunch for the slogan
desc: At a roadside tariff fair, an importer needs supplies for his public cost display. Across the aisle, a promoter offers your crew some food to repeat “China paid.” The importer has his American bank statement. The promoter has better sandwiches.

choices.label: Donate supplies to the cost display

effects.log: You donate some supplies; the importer records your help. The American payment finally gets a display board as large as the foreign-payer slogan.

choices.label: Take the food; repeat the slogan

effects.log: You collect some food and repeat the slogan. The importer corrects you with his payment record. The sandwich has purchased a very small spokesperson.

choices.label: Use your paper; record the payment

effects.log: You use some supplies to document the actual payment. The importer points to his name. It has remained American throughout the promotion.

name: The approved stairs
desc: Parents invite your crew to a fourth-floor meeting about their board’s response to Trump’s anti-indoctrination order. The lift is broken. The proposed lesson teaches that complaining weakens the nation. The staircase offers several opportunities to test the curriculum.

effects.log: You climb and argue the sourced case, legs and head aching. The board asks for a more positive account of the stairs.

choices.label: Walk with parents to their picnic

effects.log: You take the hilly route, legs sore but spirits lifted. A parent marks the broken lift absent. It receives full credit for patriotism.
You leave with a quieter head and no testimony to offer. The board’s attendance sheet has discovered another supporter of the current arrangement.

name: The returning jobs lane
desc: Trump’s tariffs have a freight yard repeatedly relabelling the same imported stock. Your van reaches the queue as a pallet makes its third patriotic lap. A flagger offers a direct coned lane or an easier merge. The pallet has travelled farther than the job it’s bringing back.

effects.log: You gain road and clear your head. The flagger gets you past the queue. The pallet begins another tour of American manufacturing.
You gain road through an easy merge. The crew enjoys seeing the same pallet return to the same worker, now wearing a different flag.

name: The hydrated shortcut
desc: After DOGE park staffing cuts, the remaining ranger is routing visitors around an unattended entrance. She offers your stopped crew a short open service lane if you share some water, or the signed public loop with her account. Her radio keeps asking an empty desk for assistance.

choices.label: Share some water; take the short lane

effects.log: You share some water and gain road through the open lane. The ranger’s radio requests backup. She drinks it herself.

choices.label: Take the public loop; record her account

effects.log: You gain road and record the staffing account. The empty desk has excellent radio discipline. It never interrupts anyone.

name: Both ways to war
desc: A surplus market copied Trump’s “Department of War” secondary title onto its gate. Defence points left; War points right. Both queues meet at the same exit. Your stopped crew gets a choice from the marshal: direct cones or a quieter merge. The gate is winning on both fronts.

effects.log: You gain road through the direct lane. Behind you, Defence and War continue negotiating access to the same broken gate hinge.
You gain road and clear your head in the quiet merge. The marshal removes a duplicate arrow. A naming dispute becomes one ordinary exit.

name: A shift to prove the shift
desc: Your tired crew stops at a workshop preparing for Medicaid work checks due from 2027. A cleaner is filling in a practice form during her unpaid break. The form asks why she isn’t working. Volunteers offer a table for your own food and welcome help.

effects.log: You read until your head aches. The cleaner lists her unpaid break as time spent explaining her unpaid break. The form requests detail.

choices.label: Use some food; take a break

effects.log: You use some food and recover at the table. The cleaner turns the form face down. It cannot question chewing from that position.
You donate some supplies, and volunteers add your help to their account. The cleaner finally gets a spare pen that doesn’t belong to another job.

name: The safe place to stop
desc: After Trump officials’ Signal scandal, a roadside freight desk has put its public rest-area directions through a privacy briefing. Your tired crew is welcome to wait. The dispatcher knows a quiet corner. The briefing presenter has accidentally sent the directions to the biscuit supplier.

effects.log: You read until your head aches. The biscuit supplier knows where you can rest. The people operating the rest area await a secure reply.
You use some food and rest with a clearer head. The dispatcher closes the briefing window. The outdoor bench requires no recipient list.

choices.label: Ask the dispatcher about the quiet corner

effects.log: The dispatcher becomes a local contact and shows you a place to rest. She writes her number down without adding a journalist.

name: The adhesive boom
desc: At a grocery hit by Trump’s tariffs, your crew can buy some food for $6 or earn $10 applying revised prices. The owner has run out of shelf space for the stickers. American manufacturing has begun with a very large order of glue.

effects.log: You pay $6 and collect some food. The cashier peels off the old price. It comes away more reluctantly than the patriotic flag.
You earn $10 and a headache. By closing time, the shelf is mostly adhesive. The promised manufacturing boom has reached your thumb.
You pass and leave dispirited. The affordability display has put its own prices out of reach.

name: Actual-size science
desc: A library fair is checking the nonexistent studies from the initial MAHA report. The organizer offers your crew $8 to correct the display cards. The original author table has empty chairs. The corrected version needs actual people, which is proving a serious catering complication.

choices.label: Check and save the citation history

effects.log: You save the original and corrected references with a headache. The organizer cancels the imaginary seating plan. The room becomes smaller and more accurate.
You earn $8 and enjoy crossing out the fictional study. It is the first government-inspired job here completed without needing an imaginary qualification.
You leave dispirited. The empty author chair has acquired a ribbon. The organizer still needs somebody who exists to move it.

name: The desk survived
desc: After DOGE park firings, a campground association is moving the unused service desk into its volunteer tent. They offer your crew $12 for lifting, or welcome supplies. The coordinator calls the desk “excess bureaucracy.” It still has to go somewhere people can ask for toilet paper.

effects.log: You donate some supplies and gain a local contact. The coordinator finds your details easily; the desk’s staff directory has plenty of space.
You earn $12 with aching arms. The coordinator empties the drawer of unused name badges. Smaller government becomes surprisingly easier to lift.
You leave dispirited. The empty service desk remains outside the volunteer tent, continuing its successful transition out of public service.

name: The foldout electorate
desc: A roadside café hosts a bookkeeper’s public guide to unlimited super-PAC money; some food costs $5. Your crew stops beside a sample donor ledger. The ordinary voter fits on a receipt. The billionaire requires a foldout that has reached the next table.

choices.label: Check and save the spending rules

effects.log: You save the checked rules and examples, head aching. The bookkeeper folds the billionaire away. Several ordinary voters become visible underneath.
You pay $5 and collect some food. The cook gives your order equal time on the grill. The ledger’s largest donor has not been consulted.
You leave dispirited. The bookkeeper opens another foldout. The electorate is going to need a larger tablecloth.

name: Patriotically air-conditioned
desc: Florida barred local heat-break rules. At a roadside trade fair, a contractor wants the same freedom here. He praises toughness from inside a refrigerated sales trailer. A worker points you toward shade; the trailer’s exhaust is blowing directly onto her.

effects.log: Food and shade restore you. The contractor shuts his trailer window to explain more comfortably why workers need fewer protections.
His certainty calms you. You repeat it; the worker offers to swap places with his air conditioner. Your authority evaporates.
You leave irritated. The contractor puts on a cardigan before recording another message about people becoming too sensitive to heat.

name: The drain is unpatriotic
desc: Trump ordered “Gulf of America” onto federal maps. At a flooded parking stop, the owner offers $7 to repaint his sign. The attendant asks for a drain. He hands her a flag.

effects.log: Seven dollars and a headache. The owner salutes the new gulf while you wring the old water out of your socks.
Drivers trust your arrow. The attendant asks whether draining an American gulf now counts as surrendering territory.
You leave disappointed. His flag falls into the puddle. He blames Mexico.

name: The raccoon has seniority
desc: After DOGE’s park-staff cuts, you stop at a park-side shop. The clerk offers $9 to fold trail leaflets. Outside, a bin overflows beneath AMERICA THE BEAUTIFUL. A raccoon is wearing somebody’s entire picnic.

effects.log: You share food and exchange numbers, enjoying a laugh. She locks the door before the raccoon applies for management.
Nine dollars and aching eyes. The clerk endorses your careful folding. Washington’s savings now require the gift shop’s wages.
You leave disappointed. The raccoon climbs onto the information desk, becoming the first park employee to receive lunch.

name: America First, bend from the knees
desc: Trump acknowledged deportations were taking workers from farms and hotels. At a produce yard, a manager offers $14 to move crates or food for sorting labels. His DEPORT THEM ALL sticker remains on the forklift. He has taped HELP WANTED underneath.

effects.log: Fourteen dollars and a sore back. The manager asks if you know anyone else, briefly expanding his preferred immigration policy to bring friends.
You earn supplies and a headache. The manager keeps searching the help-wanted responses for somebody his bumper sticker has not already fired.
You leave without earnings. The manager turns the forklift around so its political position stops addressing the hiring queue.

name: China’s card declined
desc: Trump says China pays the tariffs. At a roadside shop, your supplies cost $12. The cashier taps a Chinese flag against the card reader. Declined.

effects.log: Your payment works. “Congratulations,” she says. “You’re China now.”
She circles the tariff. “China’s very generous with your money.”
You leave empty-handed. The tariff has successfully protected the supplies from Americans.

name: A donation you can trip over
desc: Super PACs accept unlimited contributions. You stop at an event depot offering $10 to carry a donor’s giant ceremonial cheque. Its accompanying poster says every citizen has a voice. The cheque is too wide to fit through the citizens’ entrance.

choices.label: Save the terms and donor display

effects.log: You document the arrangement, head aching. The donor’s speech is officially independent; it still requires three people and a loading door.
Ten dollars and sore muscles. The donor signs in one effortless stroke; you need to sit down after delivering his free speech.
You leave disappointed. A worker removes the public entrance sign so the donor’s equal voice can scrape through sideways.

name: Working on proof of working
desc: Congress added Medicaid work requirements for 2027. At a community information table, a cleaner practices assembling proof of shifts between shifts. The sample form asks why she missed the workshop. Her payslip is still damp from the job that prevented her attending.

effects.log: You document the mismatch, mentally drained. The cleaner’s work prevented her proving she works. The sample answer box is admirably small.
You share food and exchange numbers. She eats while sorting payslips, providing evidence that employment can interfere with both lunch and paperwork.
You leave frustrated. She asks whether attending a workshop about proving work can itself count as work. Nobody has brought that form.

name: Cabinet-level contact management
desc: Trump’s team included a journalist in its Signal strike chat. At a café showing the news, the owner offers $8 to clear a tour bus’s tables. The cashier needs his PIN to refund mayonnaise.

effects.log: You confirm the report. The café’s new security procedure is asking who the people in the chat actually are.
Eight dollars and a headache. You match forgotten phones to passengers. The café’s standards now exceed national security’s.
You leave unpaid. The mayonnaise refund remains behind a stronger security procedure than the airstrikes.

name: Freedom reaches the tuna
desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation. At a truck stop, a celebratory display sprays the sandwich counter. The clerk offers $9 to brace it. Ordinary showers are free if you bring soap. The tuna has already exercised its freedom.

choices.label: Use your soap; take a shower

effects.log: Clean at last. On your way out, a tuna sandwich makes a determined break for the drain.
Nine dollars and aching arms. You hold freedom upright while the clerk evacuates the egg mayonnaise.
You leave unwashed. The display has liberated half the lunch menu; the remaining sandwiches are gathering on higher ground.

name: Education, some assembly required
desc: Trump directed the Education Department’s closure as far as law permits. At a school fundraiser, an organizer offers $11 to sort donated books. A volunteer is using the closure flyer to prop up a broken shelf. Finally, the policy is supporting education.

effects.log: Eleven dollars and aching eyes. You shelve the books; the closure flyer holds steady in its first successful teaching-support role.
You share lunch and a laugh. She adds another closure flyer beneath the shelf, strengthening education through repeated calls to dismantle it.
You leave disappointed. The shelf needs more support; the volunteer asks whether Washington has printed anything else about providing less.

name: Gold-standard stapling
desc: The MAHA report cited nonexistent studies. A copy shop offers $15 to collate report booklets for a public discussion. The printer says missing pages are your fault, but missing science is apparently a formatting issue. He checks your staples more carefully than the references.

effects.log: Fifteen dollars, evidence, and a headache. Every page is now attached to something real, which puts the staples ahead of several citations.
Your grand reading gets a laugh. You endorse a nonexistent paper; the printer asks whether your application to the commission is pending.
You leave disappointed. The printer checks another staple, still the only part of the report willing to hold under light pressure.

name: Federal savings, local shoulders
desc: USDA cancelled local-food purchasing funds. At a co-op loading bay, an organizer offers food for packing donated groceries or $10 for sorting delivery slips. The cancelled order is easy to lift. Everything replacing it is in crates.

effects.log: You earn supplies and a sore back. The federal savings arrive in your shoulders, considerably heavier than they looked in the announcement.
Ten dollars and a headache. Each address gets matched to food; Washington’s contribution remains a remarkably lightweight cancellation notice.
You leave without earnings. The organizer folds the cancellation into a tiny square. Unfortunately, the crates refuse to become equally efficient.

name: The sea forgot its new name
desc: Trump ordered federal maps to say Gulf of America. At a marine-supply counter, a customer demands an American refund because his old chart still says Mexico. The clerk has the order. The customer checks his shoes for foreign seawater.

effects.log: You save the actual naming change, head aching. The clerk explains that the water did not relocate; the customer looks personally betrayed by geography.
The crew laughs until you invent a maritime border change. The clerk takes the chart away before your geography reaches the fish.
You leave irritated. The customer wrings out a sock and asks whether the shop can exchange the water for the patriotic version.

name: The map has already won
desc: Albuquerque reported a federal attempt to withdraw its Rail Trail grant. At a Beltway transport-book stall, a $6 route print still shows the promised path. The clerk keeps the withdrawal notice beside it. The funding has become harder to locate than the destination.

effects.log: You keep the six-dollar print as evidence. A dotted line remains the cheapest way to deliver infrastructure without anyone having to walk on it.

choices.label: Compare the notice with the map

effects.log: You save a careful comparison, head aching. The clerk draws the uncertain funding in pencil, finally giving the path an accurate surface.
You leave disappointed. The print reaches the destination beautifully; the people who might use the actual path have received a notice instead.

name: Small government inspects your straw
desc: Trump ordered federal agencies to stop using paper straws. At a burger stand, the owner films inspections of customers’ drinks as his own patriotic tribute. The cashier points out that customers are not federal agencies. He asks her to stop weakening the border.

effects.log: You share food and confirm her point. She eats while he carefully investigates whether the burger wrapper is conspiring with the straw.

choices.label: Read and save the actual order

effects.log: You save the order through a headache. His federal jurisdiction shrinks until it no longer reaches the milkshake currently in front of him.
You leave irritated. He demands another close-up of the straw, which has now received more oversight than the owner’s payroll.

name: The shower has taken the hair
desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation after years of complaining about water pressure. At a hardware launch, the demonstration blasts the wig off a presidential mannequin. The clerk offers $12 to mop; ordinary traveler showers cost $5. The wig is heading for plumbing reform.

effects.log: Twelve dollars and a sore back. You catch the wig on the mop, briefly becoming the best-groomed cleaner in the building.
Five dollars buys a proper wash. The ordinary shower leaves your hair attached, an achievement the demonstration has chosen not to emphasize.
You leave disappointed. The clerk puts the wet wig back on the mannequin, which now looks less certain about freedom.

name: Same bombs, new letterhead
desc: Trump gave the Defense Department “Department of War” as a second name. At a print shop, the printer offers $13 to sort new letterheads. He presents two invoices. “Same bombs. Twice the stationery.”

effects.log: You sort both names, save the invoices, and earn $13, head aching. The printer needs another cabinet for the expanded letterhead supply.
You announce two armies by mistake. The crew laughs; the printer doubles his quote. You both briefly understand government contracting.
You leave unpaid. The printer asks whether peace needs a separate invoice or whether nobody is ordering that.

name: The trail has become a notice
desc: Albuquerque reported a federal attempt to withdraw Rail Trail money. At a Beltway supporters’ stall, the printer offers $9 to fold leaflets. A volunteer’s bicycle leans against the funding announcement. It is the only transport here receiving actual support from the paperwork.

effects.log: You share food and gain a contact. She moves the leaflet stack under her bicycle’s wobbly stand, getting one useful public service from it.
Nine dollars and aching eyes earn an endorsement. You make the withdrawal notice compact enough for people to carry while walking.
You leave disappointed. The volunteer rings her bicycle bell; the funding notice remains considerably less capable of moving people.

name: The park is open in the photograph
desc: DOGE cut national-park staff. At a park-side concession, the owner offers $6 to hang a FULL SERVICE banner over a closed information window. A worker has the staffing notices. The owner says the photograph needs somebody helpful, preferably somebody not asking for wages.

effects.log: You document the mismatch, head aching. The helpful employee in the publicity photograph has become a cheaper substitute for someone who can answer questions.
You earn $6 and lose trust. A visitor asks the closed window for directions; the banner provides an excellent view of its own confidence.
You leave unpaid and annoyed. The owner places a cardboard ranger behind the glass. Its first shift goes exactly as well as expected.

name: The bandage exists
desc: The MAHA report cited nonexistent studies. At a community health fair, a printer offers $12 to collate discussion leaflets. A nurse can treat you with your supplies. Her bandages have an unfair scientific advantage: she can point to where they are.

effects.log: You save the error list, earn $12, and acquire a headache. Every leaflet is physically present; several things it cites remain more ambitious.
The nurse uses your supplies and patches you up. One verified source, applied directly.
You leave disappointed. The nurse opens another real bandage beside the report’s much more imaginative approach to supporting a claim.

name: The grant wants a flag
desc: Trump’s patriotic-education order reaches a school-display printer. The printer offers $12 to sort revised classroom captions. A teacher shows you the old and proposed versions: the discussion question has been replaced by a flag large enough to prevent further questions.

effects.log: You earn $12 and a headache. The flag fits perfectly over the space where a student might previously have developed an opinion.
You preserve the difference, mentally tired. The proposed lesson has one fewer question and a much more confident answer supplied in advance.
You leave the offer behind. The teacher measures the remaining discussion space, which is now chiefly the gap beneath the flagpole.

name: The campaign for a path needs a van
desc: Albuquerque reported an attempted federal withdrawal of Rail Trail funds. At a coastal transport meeting, an organizer offers $15 to deliver campaign materials using your own packing supplies. A commuter has the correspondence. Once again, the working route belongs to somebody else.

effects.log: You spend supplies and earn $15. The posters promising movement reach the meeting because the van never waited for the funding announcement.

choices.label: Compare the correspondence with the commuter

effects.log: You gain evidence and a contact, head aching. The promised path currently moves most efficiently when printed small enough for somebody to carry.
You leave the offer behind. The organizer checks your van’s departure time with more urgency than the campaign’s map has ever received.

name: Science would like a room
desc: Trump’s NIH overhead-cap proposal put research facilities’ running costs at risk. At a laboratory open day, $14 is offered for sorting equipment tags. A nurse offers basic care using shared supplies. The funding display celebrates experiments while treating their building as a suspicious luxury.

choices.label: Sort tags; save the budget comparison

effects.log: Fourteen dollars earned; your eyes ache. The refrigerator’s tag identifies an essential instrument, despite its scandalous habit of needing electricity.
You recover and gain a contact. The nurse uses an actual room, quietly committing several of the proposal’s less glamorous expenses.
You leave the offer behind. A researcher closes the door so the experiment can continue benefiting from the controversial invention of indoors.

name: The wind has not read the order
desc: Trump paused new federal wind-project approvals. At a turbine-repair stall, a technician offers $10 to sort spare-part labels. He keeps the order under a paperweight. The breeze removes the paperweight’s supporting documents every time somebody praises the pause.

effects.log: Ten dollars and a headache. The technician retrieves another page from the hedge; wind continues producing results without waiting for the speech to finish.
You gain evidence and a contact, mentally tired. He distinguishes paused approvals from moving air, a distinction the flying order demonstrates repeatedly.
You leave the offer behind. A speaker asks someone to hold the paperwork still while he explains the advantages of stopping wind development.

name: The tank has run out of freedom
desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation. At a desert service stop, a celebratory display is draining the tank. The plumber offers water for help shutting it off or $12 for the heavier work. The owner asks whether the empty tank is refusing to cooperate politically.

choices.label: Help shut it off; take water

effects.log: You gain water and some peace of mind. The plumber demonstrates the off switch, a technology omitted from the freedom ceremony.
Twelve dollars and sore muscles. You haul the equipment while the owner asks whether refilling the tank counts as government interference.
You leave the offer behind. The display coughs; the owner checks the banner instead of the water level.

name: The flag is not a customs form
desc: Trump says tariffs make foreigners pay. At a wholesale depot, $16 is offered to sort shipment labels. The owner puts American flags over imported-stock markings. The dispatcher has the original invoices. The flags have shown no interest in paying the tariff either.

effects.log: Sixteen dollars and a headache. Every flag is removed long enough for the box’s actual origin to become inconvenient again.
You save the contradiction through aching eyes. The tariff arrived in dollars payable here, despite the owner’s best efforts to give it a foreign address.
You leave the work behind. The owner adds a larger flag, increasing the box’s patriotism without reducing its bill.
